rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a contest, including a race to finish first.

example.english: We have a race tomorrow, so remember to arrive early.
example.traditional: 我哋聽日有場比賽，記住早啲到。
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 ting1 jat6 jau5 coeng4 bei2 coi3 gei3 zyu6 zou2 di1 dou3

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for a competitive race, especially when people or vehicles are trying to beat one another.

example.english: I like to race my brother home.
example.traditional: 我鍾意同阿哥鬥快返屋企。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 ji3 tung4 aa3 go1 dau3 faai3 faan1 uk1 kei5

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on taking part in a race rather than on racing against a particular opponent.

example.english: I will race in the competition this year.
example.jyutping: gam1 nin4 ngo5 wui5 caam1 gaa1 bei2 coi3

rows.note: Use this specifically when the race involves driving or racing cars.

example.english: They go to Zhuhai to race cars on weekends.
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 zau1 mut6 heoi3 zyu1 hoi2 coi3 ce1

rows.note: Use this for a human group distinguished by shared heritage or ethnicity, rather than for a sporting contest.

example.english: This race has its own language.
example.traditional: 呢個種族有自己嘅語言。
example.jyutping: nei1 go3 zung2 zuk6 jau5 zi6 gei2 ge3 jyu5 jin4

rows.note: Use this colloquial verb when someone hurries or goes extremely fast, such as racing home or racing for the door.

example.english: As soon as the bell rings, the students race out of the classroom.
example.traditional: 落堂鐘一響，啲學生就飛出課室。
example.jyutping: lok6 tong4 zung1 jat1 hoeng2 di1 hok6 saang1 zau6 fei1 ceot1 fo3 sat1
